    Coverage by finite endpoint-word intervals #

    Besides its lower and upper boundary subspaces, an endpoint word transports the zero and whole source spaces. A vector lying in the transported whole space but outside the transported zero space can be followed down the finite source-extension tree: membership in the lower boundary forces the positive child, while failure of membership in the upper boundary forces the inverse child. Both moves preserve the invariant and strictly increase word length. The uniform finite-word bound therefore forces the process to stop inside an actual word interval.
